title: Consolidate trace exporters and slim observability dependencies; optimize hot-path metrics
creator: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Over time we've accumulated multiple tracing exporters (OTLP, legacy JSON/http, and a debug-only noop) and a heavy-weight metrics library that contribute to increased cold-start time, larger server binaries, and unpredictable CPU spikes on hot inference paths. This ticket consolidates exporters, removes unused telemetry adapters, and rewrites the hot-path metrics emission to a lightweight lock-free counter for common token emit flows. Goal is reduced p50/p95 CPU on RPC worker process, smaller runtime images, and fewer OTel-related dependency CVEs to manage.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Single canonical OTLP exporter used in production runtime; legacy exporters removed behind feature flags and later deleted.
2) End-to-end trace sampling and span propagation unchanged for 99% of requests (validated by trace diffing).
3) Hot-path token emission CPU p95 reduced by at least 30% in bench harness.
4) Runtime image size decreased by at least 8% after dependency slimdown.
5) No regression in unit/integration tests; observability e2e smoke passes.
6) Deprecation notes and migration guide published in Confluence.
plan:
- Inventory current exporters and adapters across runtime, gateway, and SDKs.
- Add a compatibility shim that routes legacy span formats to OTLP for a 2-week canary.
- Extract heavy metrics aggregation from hot path into async flush path; replace counters with a minimal atomic counter implementation.
- Perform dependency upgrades: bump opentelemetry-js to 1.21.0, replace metrics reporter with lightweight in-house shim.
- Run perf harnesses (token emission, batching, KV cache hit) to measure before/after.
- Roll out canary to 10% traffic, monitor latency/cpu/trace-coverage, then do full rollout.
- Remove feature-flagged legacy exporters after 2 full cycles without incident.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: Feature-flag shim enabled in canary runtime image; route 10% traffic and collect traces.
Phase 2: If stable for 48 hours and no error budget burn, promote to 50%.
Phase 3: Full rollout with monitoring thresholds for automatic rollback.
Phase 4: Remove legacy exporter code and dependencies in a follow-up cleanup PR.
risks:
- Incompatibility with third-party monitoring integrations that depend on legacy payload shape.
- Token emission rewrite could introduce subtle counters mismatch (affects billing/usage dashboards).
- Dependency bumps might require additional changes in downstream SDKs.
- Rollout could expose increased tail-latency if async flush interacts poorly with backpressure.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for shim translation and atomic counters.
- Integration tests: span propagation across runtime->console->dashboard.
- Perf bench: synthetic token streams at 100/500/1000 concurrent requests.
- Canary metrics: CPU, p50/p95 latency, error rate, trace sampling ratio, image size.
- Post-rollout audit: compare trace counts with historical baseline for drift.
